candidate.claim: CancelToken executor guard is inverted: it returns when no cancellation has been requested, so token.reason is never set and cancellation never fires.
candidate.title: CancelToken cancel guard inverted

verifier.reason: The guard at cancel/CancelToken.js:55 returns when token.reason is falsy (its initial state), so the assignment at cancel/CancelToken.js:60 and resolvePromise at cancel/CancelToken.js:61 are unreachable and cancellation never fires.

candidate.claim: settle resolves any response with status < 500 regardless of validateStatus result, so custom validateStatus rejecting 4xx never rejects.
candidate.title: settle bypasses validateStatus for status < 500

verifier.reason: The condition at core/settle.js:16 includes '|| response.status < 500' as an independent disjunct, so any status below 500 resolves at core/settle.js:17 even when validateStatus(status) returns false, and reject at core/settle.js:19 is only reachable for status >= 500.

candidate.claim: spread passes the array as a single argument instead of spreading it, so callback receives [arr] rather than ...arr.
candidate.title: spread does not spread array arguments

verifier.reason: The code at helpers/spread.js:26 wraps the input array in another array for apply, so callback.apply(null, [arr]) passes arr as a single argument instead of spreading its elements as callback.apply(null, arr) would.

candidate.claim: combineURLs strips trailing slashes from baseURL and leading slashes from relativeURL then concatenates without inserting '/', producing '...foobar' instead of '...foo/bar'.
candidate.title: combineURLs missing separator slash

verifier.reason: The code at helpers/combineURLs.js:22 returns baseURL.slice(0, end) + relativeURL.replace(/^\/+/, '') with no '/' separator after stripping trailing slashes at helpers/combineURLs.js:18-20, so combining 'foo' and '/bar' yields 'foobar'.

candidate.claim: buildURL keeps the '#' when stripping the fragment (slice to hashmarkIndex+1) and then appends query after '#', placing query inside the fragment.
candidate.title: buildURL appends query after hash fragment

verifier.reason: The code at helpers/buildURL.js:63 slices to hashmarkIndex+1 retaining the '#', and helpers/buildURL.js:65 then appends the serialized params after it, so a URL like 'http://x/#frag' becomes 'http://x/#?a=1' with the query inside the fragment.

candidate.claim: isAxiosError returns true for any object whose isAxiosError is undefined because it checks !== false instead of truthiness.
candidate.title: isAxiosError true for plain objects

verifier.reason: At helpers/isAxiosError.js:13 the function returns utils.isObject(payload) && payload.isAxiosError !== false, so a plain object with no isAxiosError property (undefined !== false) passes both conditions and returns true.
